Package edu.cnu.mdi.view

Class ViewPropertiesBuilder

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.view.ViewPropertiesBuilder
public class ViewPropertiesBuilder extends Object
Fluent builder for constructing the Properties used to initialize a BaseView.

This is intended primarily for default view configurations, replacing the older pattern of assembling raw Object... keyVals arrays.

The builder stores values directly into a Properties instance using the same keys consumed by PropertyUtils and BaseView. Because Properties ultimately extends Hashtable, non-String values such as colors, classes, or components may be stored directly when appropriate.

Only a commonly used subset of properties is given dedicated fluent methods here. For less common properties, use put(String, Object).

    • containerClass

      public ViewPropertiesBuilder containerClass(Class<?> containerClass)
      Set the explicit container class to instantiate.

      Deprecated in favour of containerFactory(edu.cnu.mdi.view.ContainerFactory). Providing a Class requires the framework to find a (Rectangle2D.Double) constructor via reflection, which means errors surface at runtime rather than at compile time. Prefer containerFactory(ContainerFactory) for all new code.

      Parameters:
      containerClass - the container class
      Returns:
      this builder
      See Also:
      • containerFactory(ContainerFactory)

    • containerFactory

      public ViewPropertiesBuilder containerFactory(ContainerFactory factory)
      Set a ContainerFactory used to construct this view's IContainer.

      When this property is present the framework calls ContainerFactory.create(java.awt.geom.Rectangle2D.Double) instead of using the reflection-based path that previously looked for a (Rectangle2D.Double) constructor on the class stored under PropertyUtils.CONTAINERCLASS. Prefer this method for all new code because:

      • Constructor mismatches are caught at compile time, not at first use.
      • The factory can perform additional initialization that a bare constructor cannot.
      • An IDE can follow a method reference or lambda; it cannot follow a Class stored in a Properties map.

      Example:

         new ViewPropertiesBuilder()
       .title("My View")
       .worldSystem(world)
       .containerFactory(MyContainer::new)
       .build();

   // Or with extra initialization:
   .containerFactory(ws -> {
       MyContainer c = new MyContainer(ws);
       c.setGridEnabled(true);
       return c;
   })
      Parameters:
      factory - the container factory; passing null removes any previously set factory and restores the default behaviour
      Returns:
      this builder
